failureFixtureRules: append-bytes is a real instrumented append stopped before sync, not a standalone replacement implementation of the append algorithm.
A partial write leaves a measurable raw fragment tagged with the request ID; seq=0 is its observation sentinel, not a valid stored sequence.
sync-fail injects an error after bytes were written; it must not force those bytes to disappear.
recover-storage value is a controlled retained raw-prefix length. The correct fixture never removes an acknowledged durable prefix. Filesystem power-loss behavior itself is not proved.
tear-tail is an explicit fixture mutation, not a claim of natural corruption. No normal writer append follows a torn fixture until owner restart.
project-dead and recover-dead drive the production projection/reconciliation path; they must not directly manufacture an expected dead letter in the adapter.
A repeated projection is idempotent by durable terminal identity, including a crash after append and before completion.
Crash actions discard only the modeled volatile state, preserve durable records, and actually end/reconstruct the SUT lifetime.

If an internal observation, clock, failpoint, barrier, or RPC is unavailable, omit its capability and fail replay before any operation. No emulation, inferred success, skipped profile, or predicted observation is allowed.
An unowned writer append must reach the real protected SUT operation, not be rejected by adapter bookkeeping.
Adapter children stay in its POSIX process group; the runner terminates and waits on that group after each trace. Unsupported detached-child cleanup is a port failure.
initialization: op=init with first-state parameters; create a fresh temporary fixture for this trace and return result=none with actual initial observation.
limits: Focused profiles are not a proof of unrestricted cross-subsystem composition.
Existing protocol and writer suites remain required.
Safety-only bounded checks do not replace the original hardening liveness checks.
A passing adapter declaration is not independent proof of its provenance; implementation and injection seams require review.
observations: ITF-compatible values: records are objects, sequences arrays, sets use #set, functions use #map; integers may be JSON integers or #bigint.

operation.result: Exact model response category, not an unconditional ok.

observations.deadRecords: all matching durable dead-letter records, including duplicates

observations.version: authoritative committed document version; absent is 0

observations.currentTokens: issued credentials, renamed through a strict bijection
observations.kinds: actual kind metadata; both must be codex
observations.labels: actual display metadata; both are codex

observations.cursor: saved real cursor normalized to stable segment and sequence
observations.files: actual ordered segments, including empty prepared segments
observations.readBack: actual IDs returned by the cursor read
observations.records: all actual durable records with measured sizes
durable record IDs and measured encoded sizes in declared units
observations.reported: actual reported sequence head; missing nonempty head is -1

observations.receipts: Driver-owned history of actual successful API receipts; never obtained from adapter observation or reset on recovery.
observations.records: raw file records or tagged incomplete fragments; never the predicted log
observations.recoveryRequired: observed writer quarantine; may require a diagnostic test seam

observations.owners: live children responding with their own PIDs
observations.records: read-only disk scan; recovery records normalize to 99

receiptReply: On successful sync-ok, include receipt={id,seq} from the real append completion. Storage observations exclude receipts; only the driver adds its external reply history before comparison.
requiredIdentityBinding: Successful enroll/reconnect/rotate-token replies include binding={agent_id,token} from actual backend replies/authentication; both must agree with the observed actor. The runner alone binds their abstract names bijectively. Never assign synthetic IDs to clients.
scope: Instrumented implementation replay contract; does not claim a Rust adapter already exists.

sizeFixture.measurement: Total encoded record bytes including separators, not body-text length. Pad valid fixture records to the exact sizes. Oversized records occupy a segment alone; the next append rotates.

wire: One request and response per UTF-8 NDJSON line; request IDs must match; adapter receives no expected observations.
